title: A Hymn for the Smile
premise: Hazel Eriksen returns to her grandmother's decaying farmhouse to bury her twin sister Wren, only to find the death certificate bears Hazel's own name. The sisters swapped identities years ago, and the thing that answered the family's old bargain has come to collect the twin who was promised. As Hazel documents the house's impossible changes—photographs gaining an extra chair, a guest who smiles too long—she uncovers her grandmother's ledger of debts and realizes the entity can be bound by what is written, not spoken. In the final hours before dawn, Hazel rewrites the inheritance in her own hand, naming herself heir to the debt, and survives sunrise by becoming the one thing the smile cannot erase: its creditor.
about_author: Cyrus Joubert is the pen name of a former county archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing unclaimed estates in rural Norway before turning to fiction. His work explores how paper remembers what people would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Wrong Body
chapters.summary: Hazel arrives at the farmhouse for Wren's funeral and discovers the casket is labeled with her own name. Third-person limited from Hazel's POV. Emotional beat: disorientation sharpening into dread as she realizes no one will say which twin died.

chapters.title: Documentation Is a Kind of Prayer
chapters.summary: Hazel photographs every room of grandma's house, her lifelong coping ritual, but each developed image shows an extra wooden chair that isn't there. Her POV. Beat: the comfort of ritual curdling into evidence of something watching.

chapters.title: Aunt Maren Knows Better Than to Stay
chapters.summary: Aunt Maren visits briefly, refuses to enter after dark, and warns Hazel to leave before the reading of the will. Her POV via a tense kitchen scene. Beat: the first confirmation that the family shares a secret shame.

chapters.title: The Guest Room That Was Never a Guest Room
chapters.summary: Hazel finds the locked upstairs room open: a made bed, a chair facing the door, and dust undisturbed except by fresh footprints leading out. Her POV. Beat: violation—the house has been expecting someone.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Voicemail
chapters.summary: Hazel plays Wren's final message, recorded here in this house: 'It smiled at me through the window and it had your face.' Flashback chapter in Wren's voice. Beat: grief complicated by guilt over their estrangement.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Beneath grandma's bed, Hazel finds a ledger recording payments across three generations—dates, names, and a column labeled simply 'smiles.' Her POV. Beat: the horror acquires history; this is an inheritance.

chapters.title: Mr. Voss Calls on Tuesday
chapters.summary: A courteous stranger arrives claiming to be the estate's appraiser, but his reflection lags half a second behind him. Hazel's POV. Beat: polite menace; she must host the thing without letting it learn her name.

chapters.title: What Grandma Signed
chapters.summary: In the church archive, Hazel reads grandma's 1968 contract: a life granted in exchange for 'the twin born under the wrong star.' Third person. Beat: Hazel understands the promise was always about her and Wren both.

chapters.title: The Photographs Rearrange Themselves
chapters.summary: Overnight, every family photo now includes the extra chair—and in the oldest ones, a smiling figure stands behind grandma. Hazel's POV. Beat: the past itself is being rewritten around the debt.

chapters.title: Maren's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren returns, drunk and terrified, admitting she once tried to pay the debt with her own daughter and was refused—the thing wants twins specifically. Her POV. Beat: inherited sin made intimate; Hazel forgives her anyway.

chapters.title: Nine Hours Until Sunrise
chapters.summary: The power fails at dusk. Mr. Voss takes up residence in the guest room chair and announces, gently, that collection begins at dawn. Hazel's POV. Beat: the siege structure locks into place; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Hazel tests the ledger's marginal notes: don't answer to your name, don't accept gifts, don't look away from the smile. Each rule costs her something to verify. Her POV. Beat: agency through discipline; she becomes a scholar of her own haunting.

chapters.title: The Smile in the Hallway Mirror
chapters.summary: At midnight, Hazel's own reflection begins smiling independently, wearing Wren's expression. She covers every mirror in the house. Her POV. Beat: identity itself becomes contested territory.

chapters.title: An Offer, Politely Made
chapters.summary: Voss offers Hazel a trade: sign the estate over and walk away alive, leaving the debt to whoever inherits next. Her POV. Beat: temptation—justice outside the law would just mean passing the harm along.

chapters.title: The Chapter Grandma Tore Out
chapters.summary: Hazel reconstructs the ledger's missing page from indentations, learning grandma tried to void the contract once and failed because a signature given in fear still binds. Her POV. Beat: despair—every escape route was already tried.

chapters.title: Two Hours
chapters.summary: Voss stops pretending. Doors seal, the house breathes, and the extra chair drags itself to the head of the table where Hazel sits writing. Her POV. Beat: terror at full pitch; the documentation becomes defiance.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Hazel finally speaks the truth aloud: grandma invited it, the family fed it, and Wren died holding the door. Naming it breaks its anonymity—it falters for the first time. Her POV. Beat: catharsis; truth as weapon.

chapters.title: The Amendment
chapters.summary: In the last hour, Hazel writes a new page into the ledger: she accepts the debt willingly, as heir, on her own terms—no more twins, no more children, the line ends with her consent. Her POV. Beat: grim resolve; justice authored, not inherited.

chapters.title: Sunrise Negotiation
chapters.summary: As light enters, Voss reads her amendment and, bound by his own rules of contract, must honor it—but he demands payment in kind: her smile, permanently. Her POV. Beat: the cost made flesh; she pays it.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Days later, the will is read; the house passes to Hazel, and the guests notice she never smiles. Maren grieves beside her. Maren's POV. Beat: quiet aftermath; survival that looks like loss from outside.

chapters.title: One Chair Removed
chapters.summary: Hazel burns the guest room furniture and buries the ledger's original pages with Wren, keeping only her amendment. The photographs lose their extra chair one by one. Her POV. Beat: mourning and release braided together.

chapters.title: A Hymn for the Smile
chapters.summary: Years on, Hazel lives as the estate's last keeper, singing the hymn grandma taught her each dawn—a song that is actually a contract renewal, keeping the thing fed and bound. Final image: she smiles, once a year, on purpose. Her POV. Beat: belonging achieved on monstrous terms; peace with teeth.
